recipes.name: Classic Goulash
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon seasoned salt, or to taste

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add onion and cook 3 minutes, stirring often.
Add ground beef and cook, breaking up the meat until it is evenly browned, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook 3 minutes, stirring often.
Stir in water, tomato sauce, diced tomatoes, soy sauce, Italian seasoning, seasoned salt, and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook 5 minutes, stirring halfway through.
Stir in uncooked macaroni, cover, and simmer over medium heat until pasta is tender, 11 to 13 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat, discard bay leaves, and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Classic Goulash
raw_recipe.description: This goulash recipe is made on the stovetop with ground beef, tomatoes, herbs, and mararoni for a classic one-pot meal the whole family will enjoy.

video.description: In this video, learn how to make chef Nicole McLaughlin’s classic goulash recipe! Featuring a flavorful mix of beef, tomatoes, garlic, Italian herbs, and more, this goulash is sure to satisfy your cravings. Nicole makes this recipe easy to follow with step-by-step instructions plus helpful tips, tricks, and hack. And, with leftovers that can be stored in the fridge for up to three days, this dish works great for meal prep.

review.reviewBody: This is the classic goulash made in the mid-west, USA, not Hungarian Goulash. I grew up on this in Iowa, but we used Worchestershire sauce instead of soy sauce, no bay leaf, and a green pepper if we had one.

This is not "classic" Hungarian Goulash but it is goulash or Chop Suey depending on what part of the country you grew up. For me it was western NY and we added canned corn. Made this tonight, exactly as written, for my very picky folks and we loved it; it was a taste of my childhood. Next time I'll add Jalapeno and bell peppers.

This one is classic AMERICAN style goulash. The picture depicts it. This is a dish that was mainstay for most of us and even served at school. @Pathunt: Nicely done! I made it just as the recipe states and enjoyed it but next time around I will add a diced green pepper to the meat as it's browning and probably a shake of garlic powder to remind me of school, and LOTS of fresh ground pepper.
mrsjoedo mentioned something was missing, next time try adding chopped green pepper. To me it's not goulash unless you add it.

This made a ton..and I even cut it in half. Dinner was easy to make. I just think that the amount of seasoning is off a bit. Too salty and too much Italian Seasoning. I cut back on those to suit our taste. I also decided to cook the noodles separate, so I didn't add the extra water. Total cooking time was about 40 minutes. Thanks for sharing this recipe.

I think this recipe was edited at some point. I recall using 2 cups of chicken broth rather than 3 cups of water, and letting it simmer for 20 minutes before adding noodles. I know it was this recipe though because it’s been saved to my favorites for ages. Family agreed it didn’t taste quite as good as it used to. Original recipe was 5 stars, now it’s 4.

Two changes but this is my go-to! 😊 1- Use Worchestershire instead of soy sauce 2- I simmer everything except water and noodles for at least an hour. Then add water/noodles and follow instructions as listed.

I made due with what I had but this is pretty much no fail. I added a green bell pepper and more garlic. I only had 1 pound of lean ground beef but it was enough. I didn’t have Italian seasoning or bay leaves but did have basil, thyme and oregano which are all in Italian seasoning. I tried to curb the sodium with salt free tomatoes and beef stock and low sodium soy. We are babysitting the grandkids who never had this and gobbled it up. They called it Mac and Cheese with a hamburger because I put a little cheese on top. There’s plenty of leftovers too. Not bad for not being in my own kitchen. Definitely making again.

It was delicious! I noticed the printed recipe left out some ingredients she had included in the video. She used beef broth, but only 2 1/2 cups. She also added chopped green pepper and added in cheese at the end. It thickened up nicely with the addition of the macaroni. I will include this in my favorite recipes!

Easy and delicious. I used the slow cooker method and after reading several reviews, cut the amount of water back to 2 cups. The result is perfect, more stew-like. Interestingly, when I posted a pic on Facebook, I got some new terms for it thrown back at me....glop and slumgullion. Who knew?

I had to pass on the onion and garlic, and I used Worcestershire sauce instead of soy, black pepper and some salt and Italian seasoning and sugar! I always use sugar in any tomato based dish, cuts down the acid in the tomato mixture, simmering for a hour before adding water and macaroni!! So delicious 🤤 I also top it off after I spoon it in the bowl with shredded cheddar cheese 🧀

I made a half recipe and used half soya and half Worcestershire sauce. Half canned tomatoes and half medium salsa. Didn't have a green pepper so I left it out. Loved this and will be making it again and again
I loved it! This has the perfect seasoning and perfect instructions!!! Will definitely make this again!

After years of making the boring old goulash We found this recipe. During dinner I heard two things Mom This is So Good! And silverware hitting the bowls to scrape every bit from their bowl! This is now our go to favorite! I do sometimes put a can of corn into it. But it’s always a good and hearty meal. Thank you Pat Hunt for sharing! 🙂
Loved it. Used can of fire-roasted tomatoes

This is a staple in our house. I’m on a low sodium diet and usually use either fresh veggies or low sodium canned veggies. It does not need a massive amount of salt. The other spices make up for it. Easy, one pot meal.

This was really good! Only tweeks I made were 1. Used Beef broth instead of water 2. Added an orange pepper as well as green pepper 3. Used worcestershire instead of soy sauce. Definitely use the large elbow macaroni. Will definitely make again! :)

I substituted beef broth for the water. Also, with only half a box of macaroni, it was very soupy so I added the whole box and it was perfect. Also added 8oz shredded mild cheddar cheese at the end. Best funeral casserole we have had!
Delicious
I used moose burger as I always have lots of it, Italian tomato sauce, and added a can of mushrooms although maybe should have left out the mushrooms and substitute another vegetable.
